Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

wrong adjective and noun

morally wrong, not right

also it’s wrong to, do wrong, right and wrong, a wrong, wrong someone, injustice

classical

Cic. Fam. 15.21.5: quae cum tibi liceat, mihi nefās sit oblīvīscī
Cic. Att. 9.2a.1: quam sit turpe mē adesse … nefās esse approbāre
Traupman 409: wrong (morally), nefas

1nefās: long a (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked; Traupman 409 nefas). Fās with the negative ne-. De Vaan 203, s.v. fās: from *bʰeh₂-os, “saying”, the root of fārī and fāma.

nefās1

noun, indeclinable; nefās est with an infinitive, it is wrong to, declension

wrong, not to be done; a wrong

What the gods and decency forbid; its opposite is fās, and right and wrong together are fās atque nefās. A strong word, though Cicero uses it freely in his letters; milder is turpe est, it is shameful.

Other words

  • prāvus, prāva, prāvum — wrong, bad (the opposite of rēctus)

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 1.37: rēctē facta sōla in bonīs āctiōnibus pōnēns, prāvē id est peccāta in malīs

    Literally “crooked”. The adverb prāvē, wrongly, is the opposite of rēctē (Lewis & Short).

  • injūria, injūriae f. — a wrong done to someone, an injustice

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 189: tamen tibi ā mē nūlla orta est injūria

    To wrong someone is injūriam alicui facere (Cic. Fin. 3.71, Lewis & Short); the ablative injūriā is “wrongly, unjustly”.

  • injūstitia, injūstitiae f. — injustice

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.23: injūstitiae duo genera sunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 333

Examples

  • tū velim tua in mē studia et officia multum tēcum recordēre. quae cum tibi liceat, mihi nefās sit oblīvīscī

    I’d like you to think often of your goodness and kindness to me: you may forget them, but for me it would be wrong toCic. Fam. 15.21.5

  • quippe ubi fās versum atque nefās

    for here right and wrong are turned upside downVerg. G. 1.505

  • tamen tibi ā mē nūlla orta est injūria

    and yet you have had no wrong from meTer. Ad. 189

See also wrong, allow.
